summary.name: Surrealism is a supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection. An unusual scene is not automatically Surrealism, so the impossible action must be the defining idea.
summary.visualIdentity: Impossible scales, object relationships or gravity sit inside convincing space and lighting. One coherent dream logic is required, photorealistic or painterly. Transformations unfold calmly while composition and narrative continuity hold. The source sample shows a bird riding a bicycle in convincing light.
summary.suitableUses: Stated: single dreamlike images, and hybrids where a camera journey or staged composition carries the narrative. Catalog good-fit lists include surreal spatial passages, storytelling sequences and Punctuation Zoom. Brand films, music videos, art campaigns and openers are inferred from the combinations, not verified.
summary.limitations: Continuous-shot versions must avoid hidden cuts, camera intersecting geometry and rushed transformations. Avoid generic pastel grading, busy prop clutter and mixed rendering styles. Vortex passages are unsuitable when dense text must be read during travel. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent, so choose it from subject, lighting, composition and mood. The example tokens (#EDE5D7 background, #302D35 foreground, #617C8B and #B26E51 accents) are unapproved suggestions; gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 10.815:1; accent pairs (3.524, 3.377) are decorative only. Task-supplied exact colors override these. The source review suggests one motivated key light, tinted haze and a darker silhouette midground, but its golden-hour hues are not style rules.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Impossible transformations unfold calmly, with camera movement and deformation driven by keyframes or cached simulation. Optional motion references are 002 (vortex passage), 005 (luminous doorway, not a cursor trail), 012 (chapter handoff), 015 (storytelling) and 038 (punctuation zoom). Selecting no reference is valid. Interactive delivery may scrub prerendered frames with a play/pause option and a reduced-motion still.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the style; no fixed genre, tempo, instrument or voice is assigned. Music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience or silence should be proposed from topic, storyboard and motion, and explicit user audio choices take priority. No audio was verified in the sampled source frames, and motion references impose no mandatory sound.
summary.assetRequirements: Unspecified: the style itself requires no uploaded assets. Typical needs are Blender-built models, materials, lighting and cached simulations, plus local fonts and textures loaded before rendering. Punctuation Zoom requires an inspected actual mark or glyph asset. A Vortex passage may need a Three.js or PixiJS layer.
summary.combinations: Style-099 (continuous camera path through impossible spaces, Blender, cached motion) suits brand films, music videos and openers; keep one dream logic, non-resetting light and the reference palette. Style-104 (centered frontal symmetry with slow push-in) suits art campaigns and poster frames; avoid clutter and mixed rendering. Use hybrids only when a camera journey or staged composition carries the narrative.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: Blender with Python bpy and Cycles (or EEVEE) owns geometry, materials, lighting and offline renders. Motion engine: Blender keyframes or cached simulation owns transforms and deformation, with one owner per property. HyperFrames is the default for composition, timing, audio sync and export; Remotion is only a documented fallback. chroma.js optionally validates colors and contrast. Verify direct, forward and backward seeks plus decoded frames.
